answer: A key enters only with a dated silt core. The applicant locks 16.4 POA and drives a 10-byte core pin beside one mapped juniper stand on the river delta. For 28 straight blocks they post a 6-byte silt hash every fourth block, only while the official flood staff sits between 1.1 and 1.4 meters. A highland haven clerk recomputes the pin ID from the epoch seed and enforces the one-stand cap. Raising 3,100 aliases needs 3,100 unshared stands and 21,700 in-band hashes. A skipped hash, a second pin on the same stand, or a reused core burns 66% of the lock and closes that stand for eleven epochs.
